title: acs verifier verdict
description: The verifier's verdict for one iteration (MAR-527), written by the verifier and validated by the SubagentStop hook. NOTE: the invariant that makes this a verdict rather than a self-report -- `passed` must equal "no blocking finding" -- is NOT expressible here and is enforced by acs_lib.verdict.validate_verdict, which is what the hook actually runs. This schema pins the shape; that function pins the meaning.

lens.description: The full-depth review lens this verdict covers, or null for a single-pass (light-depth) verdict and for the merged one.

passed.description: DERIVED, never asserted: true exactly when `findings` carries no entry with severity `blocking`.

merged_from.description: Present only on a merged verdict: the lenses it was built from.

result.description: `n/a` is a real answer: dimension 14 is full-depth only, 15 is inactive without an approved plan, 2 and 3 are n/a under docs_only.

evidence.description: The command run and its relevant output, or the file:line the judgement rests on.

severity.description: Only `blocking` decides the verdict; `info` is reported and carried, never gating.

tests.description: The verifier's own run of the full unit suite (dimension 2), as numbers rather than prose. /acs:code runs that suite once, in verify; the executor iterates against the tests its change touches. states.tests is derived from here, so the recorded result is the review's independent finding rather than the executor's self-report. Optional: a docs-only ticket has no coverage to record, and a run can end before any verifier writes a verdict -- acs_lib.derive_tests falls back to the execute reports then.

coverage.description: Coverage read off the SAME run recorded in `tests` (dimension 3), not a second one: on most repos the test command reports coverage because it is the command the coverage gate runs. `percent` is the measured figure; the target it is judged against comes from settings.test_coverage_percent, never from here.
